name: Thalyren's groves and the highland plains
era_span: Unstated on all seven cards, and no archived scene holds any of them; the cluster note placing Gorrum in two scenes with Hild's coalition rests on a false match with the Keth-Gorrum. The only order the cards give is their chapter arcs (Chapters XI to XVIII), with the Verdant Pass Accord in Chapter XIV. Thalyren's card calls him ancient and makes him functionally immortal inside the Everbloom's domain; everyone else lives one life in one era. No year is stated.

members.line: Thalyren Veyroot · The Verdant Sentinel. He is Green-Warden of the Ninefold Grove and Rootkeeper, and his card names him "Ancient Wellspring Guardian. Grove Sovereign. Verdure Archon's Chosen." For the Sacred Conclave he is the bound protector of the Everbloom Wellspring, which his card counts among the most stable and sacred in the Core World. He holds spiritual authority over the druids, beastfolk and nature-attuned Concord members of its territory. He once walked toward the thing that could end him. He rooted. His soul is anchored to the Everbloom, and inside its domain any destruction of his body regrows from the Wellspring's roots over several days. Outside it his life-force fades, and he has to draw what he can from soil and sunlight. His card puts the cost in three words: "He cannot leave." Through his antlers he sees every grove, forest and sacred green-space in his reach, and a disturbance shows to him as leaves withering. His cloak is alive, leaf and moss and flower, and it can entangle, shed healing pollen or harden into bark. He has almost never needed to strike, and he cannot run. His card leaves one thing open: "Whether the rooting was his choice or the Everbloom's."

Lyraen Callivane · Verdure Hoof. She is called the Meadow's Whisper and Shepherd's Fang: plainswanderer, herbalist-marksman and Wellspring Mediator of Verdant Pass. An Independent Concord Freeholder, she "Holds roaming rights between Innerworld grassland settlements and Outer World frontier hamlets" and "Often acts as an unofficial emissary between Beastkin herding clans and Concord Guild parties." Her presence soothes beasts and dulls hostile intent in people, and it works best on a stampede or a mob. Her horns keep a struck note and let it out later as a burst of sound or a signal heard far off. Standing barefoot in fertile soil she mends wounds and fatigue in herself and others. Her working fails her on sterile ground, in hard cold and in exhausted earth. She shoots well and hits lightly. She once healed Varek Ka'ruun after a battle, and he called her "the little lamb that bites." Her epigraph: "Not all shepherds carry crooks. Some carry teeth." Her card leaves her Spirit Axis unnamed.

Gorrum Vaelseth · Toad Guy. He is the Croak in the Rain and the Verdant Trickster: wandering relic-broker, Wellspring cartographer, herbalist and minor hex-weaver. He is nomadic and "Loosely connected to the Guardians of Tres Aures through old pacts". He trades in rare herbs, spirit-potions and magical debris scavenged "from forgotten battlefields and collapsed Wellsprings." He is a mapmaker before anything else. In marsh, grass or shallow water he can hold still for hours until the ground hides him, and he lives by never being where a fight is. A croaking undertone in his voice inclines a listener to trust him. Every hex he makes is bound beforehand into a charm of gathered swamp herbs, since he cannot make one on the spot. His own Wellspring is a wetland that grows slowly and serves him only where it already stands. Varek Ka'ruun says Gorrum once tried to sell him "swamp air" in a bottle. Gorrum denies it, smiling. "Frogs see the ripples long before the storm hits. Sit with me. We'll wait for the flies to come to us."

Moryn Sporetail · Mushroom Fox. Moryn is the Walking Cap and Lantern-Forager: travelling sporemancer, fungal alchemist and wilderness merchant. An Independent Concord-Aligned Trader, Moryn "Wanders between Core World villages, Innerworld groves and Outer World fringes", selling potions, poultices and rare fungi for stories, maps and peculiar artifacts. Moryn "Maintains friendly ties to the Verdant Sentinel's Circle and to Gorrum Vaelseth." The spores and fungi of Moryn's cap light dark places, keep off some predators, and leave hostile creatures drowsy or seeing things. The Pouch of a Hundred Spores holds powders for growth, corrosion, healing and pestilence, every one made in advance. Moryn can listen to a region's fungal networks for recent movement, changes in weather and disturbance. Moryn's own Wellspring is a cavern of lit mushrooms and knotted roots where every living thing is at last taken into the weave, and Moryn walks in it. "Everything rots… but rot is just another way of saying 'new life begins.'"

Garruk Stonehoof · The Iron-Mane. He is the Horn of the Highlands and Hoofbreaker: centaur warlord, battlefield commander, and Wellspring Guardian of the Iron Plains. He is chieftain and spiritual protector of the Stonehoof Herdclan, "one of the oldest and most feared centaur war-hosts in the Outer World's rolling warplains," and the Hoof-Seer Wellspring chose him to guard its power. His card holds the two offices as one: "A grazing path is a grazing path and is also a sacred boundary". Stone hardens his hide and his horse's body against blades, arrows and some glyph-work, and he does not break stride. At full gallop his charge breaks formations, barriers and wards. His voice rallies a herd or panics a foe across a battlefield. Inside his Wellspring he gives the herd its battle-lust and then has to command the herd that has it. He needs open ground and a run. Broken terrain and a feint beat him. "Steel rusts. Stone crumbles. But the hoof leaves its mark forever."

Kaelen Brighthoof · The Horned Hawk. He is the Arrow of the Peaks: highland tracker, Wellspring path-guide and hunter of Outer Realm beasts. His people are the Hornclimb Clan, "a Beastkin clan living in the high mountain passes between the Core World and Outer World fringe realms", scouts and defenders for travellers crossing dangerous alpine Wellspring country. He crosses sheer rock under fire without losing his footing. He can slow his breath and heartbeat until he is nearly impossible to detect. His arrows land by placement. The goats, hawks and horned deer of his home range are soul-bound to him and scout or carry messages on a hunt. His Wellspring is a mountain peak. He must be on the mountain, where altitude and cold are his ground, and the flatlands beat him. "From up here, the wind carries every lie, every footstep, every chance to put an arrow where it matters."

Cernan Eryndor · The Bull. He is the Ironblood Rampart, "Unaligned Warden of the Outer World," with "Rumoured descent from the Eryndor bloodline of Lowmere." A presence his card calls the Raging Bull is resident in his Crystal. Nobody worships it or summons it, and what it is waits on a ruling. His method is mass in a straight line. His charge makes a whole formation, wall or gate give at once, and the blow carries through the first body into whatever stands behind it. He holds together through the exertion. Afterward he sleeps, and nobody can wake him. His card gives him one way to lose: "every commander who has beaten him has beaten him with one", a feint. The year of his Catalyst "was the worst year of his life and he has never described it." His card names no one.

events.name: The grove on the Stonehoof path
events.when: Undated, and new. After Thalyren rooted himself to the Everbloom, which is his card's Catalyst Event. It falls in one grazing season of the Stonehoof Herdclan under Garruk, while Moryn was a guest of the Ninefold Grove.
events.where: A sacred grove at the outer edge of Thalyren's sight about the Everbloom Wellspring, where a Stonehoof grazing path runs through it (Thalyren's and Garruk's cards). His card sets the Everbloom in the Core World, which no page places among the four quarters (WORLD §3; section 7). The herd came up to the grove from its warplains in the Outer World (Garruk's card; WORLD §3).
events.what: One grazing season the Stonehoof Herdclan came up its path and through a sacred grove at the edge of Thalyren's sight. The herd grazed as it went. It cropped the understory to the roots and trod the leaf-mould into mud. Thalyren saw the grove as his sight shows him any disturbance, as leaves withering. He stayed at the Everbloom. Moryn, a guest in the grove that season, went out in his place, knelt in the trodden ground and listened to the mycelium under it. The network held many hooves on one line, a herd on its road, and nothing cut or burned. Moryn carried that back. Thalyren sent word to the herd by Lyraen, whose roaming rights run into the Outer World and who goes between herding clans and those who deal with them. She walked barefoot into the Stonehoof camp and put his word to Garruk. Garruk heard her out. The path was the herd's, and a sacred boundary under the Hoof-Seer Wellspring, and he would not move it. He gave her the herd's answer in his own words: "Steel rusts. Stone crumbles. But the hoof leaves its mark forever." He agreed to one thing. The herd crossed the grove at a walk, did not graze inside it, and went on over the season. Moryn told Thalyren the trodden ground would feed the next growth. The understory was back before the herd returned. What each took: Thalyren took a grove he watched wither from the Everbloom and did not walk to, and a boundary another warden holds sacred running through his own. He did not strike. Garruk took the path, kept, and his word to walk it where it crosses the grove. Lyraen took the go-between's part between the grove and the herd, and it falls to her each time the path and the groves meet again. Moryn took a reading of the ground that both wardens accepted, and a guest's standing that now includes being sent.

events.name: The Verdant Pass Accord
events.when: In the arc Lyraen's card names "The Verdant Pass Accord" and Gorrum's card names "Trade at the Verdant Pass", both in Chapter XIV. No era is stated. The gathering is the cards'. Its terms, and the people at it beyond Lyraen and Gorrum, are new.
events.where: The Verdant Pass, of which Lyraen is Wellspring Mediator (her card). No page places it. Her roaming rights run between Innerworld grassland settlements and Outer World frontier hamlets (her card; WORLD §3).
events.what: Beastkin herding clans drove their herds through the Verdant Pass in their season, and in the same weeks a Concord Guild party came up to draw on the pass's Wellspring. Hornclimb scouts had guided the party through the high passes. Kaelen came down with them. Lyraen, as the pass's Wellspring Mediator, called the clans and the party to the meadow under the Wellspring. Gorrum came up the pass to trade, last of anyone. Lyraen called him Old Croak for it in front of both sides. He had mapped the pass and its Wellspring on an earlier road, and the clans and the party both knew his map. They agreed to write the terms against it. The clans kept the pass in their season, and the Guild party drew on the Wellspring outside it. Lyraen put her name to the terms as mediator. Moryn came through during the gathering and traded refined spore-powders for Gorrum's swamp herbs and rare fungi for Lyraen's Harmony herbs. Moryn also took a tracing of Gorrum's map as part of a price. On the last evening Lyraen and Kaelen shot at marks across the meadow, she from the grass with her feet bare in the soil, he from the rock above it, shooting down. Afterward they traded techniques. He teased her for "fighting in flatlands." What each took: Lyraen took the Verdant Pass Accord, with her name beside both parties'. Gorrum took his trade, and a map that is now the record both sides point to when they disagree. Kaelen took a guiding fee for his clan and a contest. Moryn took herbs, a tracing of the pass and the stories that came with it, which are the currency Moryn prefers.

events.name: The watch on the warplains
events.when: Undated, and new. It falls in one of the dangerous hunts Kaelen scouted for the Stonehoof Herd (Garruk's card), while Cernan held his unaligned wardenship of the Outer World.
events.where: The Stonehoof Herdclan's warplains, in the Outer World (Garruk's card; WORLD §3). No page places the Iron Plains or the herd's range more closely.
events.what: An Outer Realm beast came down out of the high country onto the Stonehoof warplains. Garruk took the herd out after it, with Kaelen scouting ahead along the ridges. Cernan met the beast first. He was warding that ground on nobody's commission, and he charged it across the open plain in a straight line. The beast was out of the line when the charge arrived. The charge ran on through empty ground and ploughed a furrow in it. At the end of the furrow Cernan went down asleep, as he does after that charge, and nothing woke him. From the ridge Kaelen found the furrow, the sleeping man at its end, and the beast's track bending back toward him. He sent a hawk to the herd. Garruk brought the Stonehoof up and set them in a ring about the sleeping man, on open ground where a charge has its run. He held the herd there through the day and did not go after the beast. At dusk it came back for the man. Kaelen lay still on the rock with his breath slowed and put an arrow where it mattered. The herd ran the beast down on the open ground before it reached the ring. Cernan woke inside the ring. The hunt was over. What each took: Cernan took a debt to the Stonehoof Herdclan he did not ask for, and one more loss of the old kind: what he charged was not in the line. Garruk took the kill, and a warden of the Outer World in the herd's debt, bought with a day of standing still. Kaelen took the hunt he had tracked and the arrow he placed. He also took what he saw at the end of the furrow: the warden asleep, and beyond waking.

ties.summary: He treats her as a favoured child of the grove and guides her in Harmony rituals, and she carries his word out of the grove where he cannot follow.
Thalyren's card calls Gorrum an old acquaintance and says nothing more.
Moryn is welcome in the Ninefold Grove for their respect for growth and decay, and went out as the grove's reader when the herd crossed the rim.
Each holds a boundary sacred and the two cross; Garruk respects him, kept his path, and crosses the grove at a walk.
Kaelen respects him as a guardian and prefers the hunt to guarding.
She calls him Old Croak and teases him for his slow pace.
Harmony herbs for fungi only Moryn can cultivate.
Archery contests and traded techniques, and his standing jibe about fighting in flatlands.
She walked into the Stonehoof camp with Thalyren's word and came back with the path kept and crossed at a walk.
His swamp herbs for Moryn's refined spore-powders, and a tracing of his Verdant Pass map.
Kaelen scouts for the Stonehoof Herd in dangerous hunts.
The Stonehoof stood in a ring over the warden through a day while he slept past waking on their warplains.
Kaelen found him asleep at the end of his own furrow and sent for the herd.

outward.wants: An officer of Wellspring law who comes to him, since he cannot go to anyone: Lord Maerion Lysandre, whose card says he "Works closely to ensure Wellspring laws are upheld in natural realms."
The Concord Guild party officer on the other side of her emissary's work, the one who signed the Verdant Pass terms and deals with the herding clans through her.
A keeper of the Guardians of Tres Aures, the other party to the old pacts his card says loosely bind him; no page describes the order.
A healer in one of the Core World villages on Moryn's round, who buys the poultices and pays in stories.
An officer of the Black Concord, whose outpost his card names in the arc "Siege of the Black Concord Outpost"; the card does not say which side of its wall he stood on.
A Hornclimb elder, the keeper of the clan's passes who sends him out and answers for the clan's guiding.
A commander who has beaten him with a feint, since his card says every commander who has beaten him did it that way.

card_contradictions: Who names whom among the four. Moryn's card: "Thalyren, Lyraen, Gorrum and Moryn all know each other, all work Verdantia, and all four cards name at least two of the others." Thalyren's card names two of the others, Lyraen and Gorrum, and not Moryn. Lyraen's card names one, Gorrum. Gorrum's card names one, Lyraen.

Lyraen's Spirit Axis. Thalyren's card: "This may be Lyraen's missing Spirit Axis.", with Thalyren "the strongest candidate on the board" and "stronger than Gorrum". Gorrum's card: "The obvious reading is that they are each other's, and neither card says so." Lyraen's card: "The Axis is not identified, which is worth knowing before she is written." Left open; no event here names her Axis.

Lurien. Thalyren's card, heading note: "the Sacred Conclave of Lurien, third instance in this batch." WORLD.md §3 strikes the Holy See of Lurien. RULINGS.md, 2026-09-12: "The Holy Sea of Alabaster inherits the Holy See of Lurien's old jurisdiction over southern phosphate law, along with everything else it replaced." Seraphion Veydrak's card: "Thalyren, Gonju and Chimwala are all anchored to it." and "One re-homing ruling to the Holy Sea of Alabaster settles all five". No ruling names the Sacred Conclave. This record writes it as his Affiliation line does, "Sacred Conclave", and places it nowhere.

The Core World. Thalyren's, Moryn's and Kaelen's cards name it: "one of the most stable and sacred in the Core World"; "Core World villages, Innerworld groves and Outer World fringes"; "between the Core World and Outer World fringe realms". The four quarters are the Inner, Old, New and Outer Worlds (Geography & the Four Quarters/The Bearing and the Holding.md; WORLD.md §3), and no page places a Core World. Moryn's card lists Core World villages and Innerworld groves as two kinds of place.

Lowmere. Cernan's card: "Rumoured descent from the Eryndor bloodline of Lowmere." The Celestial Host.md makes Lowmere "Utopia's realm of buried statute and redacted history", home of the Lowmere Choir, and WORLD.md §6 gives the Host "No childhood, no lineage". Leontes Praevan's card, ruled 2026-09-12: "No Utopia tie." and "The earlier note's claim that the terms recur across Volume IV, and that Cernan Eryndor's line is named as exiles of Utopia, does not hold". The descent stays a rumour.

Gorrum in the archive (index, not card). scenes/CAST.md: "Gorrum Vaelseth (2 scenes)", from 10_wotr_what_the_ground_was_owed.md and the_revolution_of_the_inner_world.md. Every match in both is "Keth-Gorrum", the Expanse's assembly. The cluster note "Gorrum appears in two archive-present scenes with Hild's coalition" rests on it. Gorrum Vaelseth is in no scene.
